questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I chose to go on exchange to get a break from the daily rutine at home, challenge myself and meet new people.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I chose University of British Columbia because I wanted to go somewhere out of Europe and with a lot of nature. 
Canada is a extremely beautiful country and when you live in Vancouver the nature is very easy to access.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was easy enough to find information, but you shouldn't expect someone to just offer it to you, I lot of th things you have to find on your own.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When you are on exchange at UBC you are connected to their Go Global-program which helps exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
You have to put in an effort to find housing off campus. UBC has a lot of exchange students and only around 50% gets housing on campus so a lot of students a looking for a short term lease close to campus. 
I think Facebook-groups and Craiglist is the best way to find a place. 
I quickly teamed up with some other exchange students who also didn't receive housing on campus, it is a lot easier and cheaper to find a bigger place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is more expensive than living on campus and many have a long commute to campus. With that being said I think the students living off campus get to explore the city of Vancouver much more.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Registrering for classes is easy but a lot of exchange students experience that the classes are full when trying to registre as full-time students get to registre before exchange students. 
Within the first few weeks students are allowed to add/drop courses so often spots open up, you just have to be patient and check the registration site regularly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Go Global

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I am very happy with the courses I ended up in. I ended up dropping some of the courses I initially thought I wanted to follow because the material was different than I expected but then found other interesting courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at courses from home. Sign up for more classes than you need and try them up when you get here. Sign up fro classes that you can't have at home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 300- and 400-level courses. I found the level a bit lower than what I am used to at home, but then the teaching style and the way the courses are build are much different then at home so it is hard to compare directly and you spend some time learning the new way of study.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I have only had lectures on UBC and no tutorials which I am used to having at home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Economics of Non-Renewable Resources
The Process of economic Development
Sex and Gender in the Economy
Economic History of Modern Europe

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed Economics of Non-Renewable Resources and Sex and Gender in the Economy.

questions.answer: I was surprised by the general price level in Canada. It is the same/a little higher than in Denmark.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything, there is a club for almost every kind of activity.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use the sport facilties! They are free or very cheap and it is a fun way to get to know people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the nature. The mountains are just around the corner.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go on trips.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Canadian people are very friendly and welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring a sleeping bag, a good pair of shoes and skiing gear.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of Danish exchange students at UBC. I didn't mind it, it is nice some times to be around people who speak the same language, but you don't get the same feeling of being completely on your own.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being around people who, just like yourself, wants to get to know new people and explore a new country,

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding the balance between academic work and fun experiences.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
